# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-2 (Extended v46)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion and Bombarda's restaurant); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; Valjean enters courtroom; WITNESSES TESTIFY; Valjean rises and reveals himself; DEPARTS COURTROOM; ARRIVES AT INFIRMARY NEXT MORNING AT DAYBREAK; CHAMPMATHIEU ACQUITTED; ARREST ORDER ISSUED; JAVERT ARRIVES AT INFIRMARY ANTECHAMBER)**; 1862 (narrative reflection); present day (spring to late August/early September, England); future wedding (following spring); 1795 (Valjean's theft and trial)
- Primary locations: M. sur M., Montfermeil, Arras (Hotel de la Poste, Court of Assizes in Prefecture, council-chamber, courtroom with corridors, steps, gratings, door, audience hall); infirmary (laboratory, Fantine's chamber, Hall of Assizes corridor); England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby)
- **Journey and courtroom entry (completed)**: Valjean hired Scaufflaire's tilbury; departed M. sur M. night of January 1823; arrived Arras nearly eight o'clock evening; left alone in council-chamber; fled corridor in terror; re-entered courtroom despite fear; concealed face behind cardboard boxes; gradually recovered composure sufficient to listen.
- **Trial proceedings and testimony (completed)**: Champmathieu (accused) made incoherent denials; Ex-convict Brevet testified (age sixty, recognized Valjean as galley companion entered 1796 left 1815); Prisoner-for-life Chenildieu (red cassock, green cap, fifty years old, nicknamed "Je-nie Dieu"); Prisoner-for-life Cochepaille (peasant from Lourdes, brigand).
- **Valjean's courtroom revelation (completed)**: Man (Valjean) rose among spectators, pushed through half-door, stood in middle of hall; **his gray hair had turned entirely white during the hour he sat in courtroom**; clerk's lamp illumined countenance; audience experienced indescribable sensation; Valjean advanced towards witnesses; addressed Chenildieu directly with specific knowledge of burn mark on right shoulder and T.F.P. letters from chafing-dish coal attempt to efface them.
- **Courtroom aftermath and acquittal (completed)**: Chamber contained no longer judges, accusers, gendarmes; only staring eyes and sympathizing hearts; no question put, no authority intervened; all felt inwardly dazzled; Valjean departed courtroom with divine something causing crowd to part; district-attorney, recovering from shock, deplored "mad deed" but found sentiments of public, court, and jury against him; counsel for defence established Champmathieu innocent in light of Valjean's revelations; President summed up in favour of acquittal; jury freed Champmathieu within minutes.
- **Legal response and arrest order (completed)**: After Champmathieu's liberation, district-attorney and President conferred "as to the necessity of seizing the person of M. le Maire of M. sur M." (phrase written by district-attorney on minutes of report to attorney-general); President did not object strongly; Justice must take its course; President (kindly, tolerably intelligent, devoted and ardent royalist) had been shocked to hear Mayor say "Emperor" not "Bonaparte" regarding Cannes landing; order of arrest signed by district-attorney: "Inspector Javert will apprehend the body of the Sieur Madeleine, mayor of M. sur M., who, in this day's session of the court, was recognized as the liberated convict, Jean Valjean."
- **Valjean's arrival at infirmary and Fantine's expectation (completed)**: Half-hour after midnight: Valjean quit Hall of Assizes; regained inn; engaged place in mail-wagon; arrived M. sur M. little before six o'clock morning; posted letter to M. Laffitte; entered infirmary to see Fantine; found her awake, having experienced sleepless feverish night filled with happy visions; her hair now gray (changed over two months since first visit); she is making visible effort to be calm and "very good" so they will permit Cosette's visit; **she sleeps and wakes in belief that Madeleine has gone to Montfermeil to fetch Cosette**.
- **Fantine's condition and delusions (ongoing)**: Terminal illness advanced; organic disease nearly despaired of; breathing with tragic sound of fatal maladies; countenance transfigured with ineffable serenity; pallor become whiteness; crimson cheeks; long golden lashes trembling though closed; whole person trembling with unfolding wings; resembles ascension rather than death; no longer has fever; claims to be perfectly conscious nothing the matter with her; but displaying terminal lucidity and mystical expectation; fantasies of future life with Cosette: little garden (promised by M. Madeleine); daughter playing, spelling lessons, chasing butterflies, taking first communion; hears child playing in yard (portress's child or work-woman's), singing; child's voice intermingled with Fantine's smiling thoughts; suddenly vision passes—she raises herself to sitting posture; thin shoulder emerged from chemise; radiant face becomes ghastly; fixes large terror-rendered eyes on something alarming at far end of room (**visual manifestation of approaching death or spiritual vision—text unclear**).
- **Javert's arrival at infirmary (commencing)**: Messenger (clever police member) informed Javert of Arras events in two words; Javert penetrated antechamber of infirmary; appeared to observer as most ordinary air—cool, calm, grave, gray hair smooth upon temples, mounted stairs with habitual deliberation; but observer thoroughly acquainted with him would have shuddered: buckle of leather stock was under his left ear instead of at nape of neck, betraying unwonted agitation.

## Main Characters and Relationships

**Jean Valjean / M. Madeleine—IDENTITY REVEALED, PAST CONFRONTED, NOW SOUGHT BY LAW**
- Rose in courtroom to reveal himself; hair turned white during hour of trial; addressed Chenildieu with intimate galley knowledge (burn mark, T.F.P. letters); allowed innocent man to be freed; departed with divine quality causing crowd to part; half-hour after midnight quit Hall of Assizes; arrived M. sur M. little before six o'clock morning; posted letter to M. Laffitte; entered infirmary; now present beside Fantine as arrest order circulates and Javert approaches.

**Fantine—TERMINAL ILLNESS, MYSTICAL EXPECTATION, APPROACHING DEATH**
- Sleepless feverish night of happy visions; gray hair (two-month change); making effort to be calm and "very good" to secure Cosette's visit; believes Madeleine has gone to fetch her daughter from Montfermeil; no fever; claims perfect consciousness that nothing the matter with her; fantasizes future life: little garden, daughter playing, spelling lessons, chasing butterflies, first communion; hears child playing in yard singing; suddenly experiences alarming vision (approaching death manifestation or spiritual encounter); raised to sitting; thin shoulder emerged; radiant face becomes ghastly; terror-rendered eyes fixed on alarming object at far end of room.

**Cosette** (Age ~7-8 in 1823)
- At Montfermeil with Thénardiers; subject of Fantine's delusion that Madeleine has gone to fetch her; object of mother's mystical maternal longing and future fantasies.

**Thénardier** (Cook-shop keeper, Montfermeil)
- Cook-shop keeper; continues obstruction of Cosette's departure; subject of Fantine's anxious inquiries about daughter's care and cleanliness.

**Javert** (Police Inspector, M. sur M.)
- Received arrest order from messenger; order reads: "Inspector Javert will apprehend the body of the Sieur Madeleine, mayor of M. sur M., who, in this day's session of the court, was recognized as the liberated convict, Jean Valjean"; penetrated antechamber of infirmary; appeared outwardly cool, calm, grave, gray hair smooth; but buckle of leather stock under left ear instead of nape indicates unwonted agitation; now present at infirmary awaiting Valjean.

**Courtroom Witnesses and Officials (Trial completed)**
- **Brevet** (Ex-convict, age sixty): testified Valjean as galley companion entered 1796 left 1815.
- **Chenildieu** (Prisoner-for-life): bears burn mark on right shoulder and T.F.P. letters from attempted efacement by chafing-dish coals; witnessed Valjean's specific knowledge of this mark.
- **Cochepaille** (Prisoner-for-life): peasant from Lourdes, brigand.
- **Champmathieu** (Accused): acquitted and set at liberty within minutes of Valjean's revelation and jury's deliberation.
- **President** (Court of Assizes): summation favored acquittal; later conferred with district-attorney on arrest order; did not object strongly; shocked by Mayor's use of "Emperor" instead of "Bonaparte."
- **District-attorney**: persisted in demanding Champmathieu's condemnation despite public and court sentiment; took word to deplore Valjean's "mad deed"; overridden by President's summing up and jury's swift acquittal; drafted arrest order for Valjean to attorney-general.
- **Sister Simplice** (Infirmary): watching Fantine; continues to observe her condition and Valjean's behavior.

## Themes
- **Confrontation with past and redemptive sacrifice completed; legal consequence imminent**: Valjean revealed himself, saved innocent man, departed courtroom; now arrest order circulates; Javert approaches infirmary; Fantine approaches death in mystical expectation.
- **Hair-whitening as temporal collapse and spiritual transformation**: Valjean's gray hair turned white in single hour of trial; Fantine's hair turned gray over two months; physical transformations mark invisible spiritual transformations; both approaching liminal state.
- **Mystical maternal redemption and approaching transcendence**: Fantine's sleepless night of happy visions; fantasizes future life with Cosette; suddenly experiences terrifying vision (death or spiritual encounter); trembling with unfolding wings ready to soar; body and spirit in paradoxical states—claims health while terminal, expects happiness while approaching end.
- **Justice apparatus overwhelmed then reasserting itself**: Court dissolved into sympathy; jury swiftly acquitted innocent man; but district-attorney and President immediately moved to arrest Valjean; legal machinery reasserts itself; Javert approaches with outward calm but inward agitation.
- **Atmospheric doom and inevitable convergence**: Gulls over fish heads; carts with turnips; frost silvering hedges; wind off water with salt and tar; bell for vespers; ruts and puddles after thaw; crooked sun on forge wall; bees humming; dog barking; children chasing hoop; all suggesting inexorable fate now converging at infirmary as Javert arrives with arrest order while Fantine awaits daughter and Valjean watches beside her.
